title: Insert a row and read its id
summary: After an insert in the same connection, LAST_INSERT_ID can report the automatically generated id.
introduction: After an insert in the same connection, LAST_INSERT_ID can report the automatically generated id. Your task: Insert another sample book and read its id.
learningObjectives: Insert another sample book and read its id.
Explain the example for insert a row and read its id

blocks.text: After an insert in the same connection, LAST_INSERT_ID can report the automatically generated id.

Use MariaDB 10.11+ with its mariadb client in an empty practice database. These dialect-specific examples do not run in the site's SQLite playground. Keep the sample database separate from real records.

blocks.code:
INSERT INTO cma_maria_books(title,pages) VALUES('Moon Trip',60);
SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID() AS new_book_id;
blocks.title: Insert a row and read its id

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `LAST_INSERT_ID` reads the generated id associated with this connection's insert, not a guessed global maximum.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The result is the id generated for that insert in this session.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Keep the insert and id read in the same connection. Do not use the largest id from all sessions as a guess.
